literal: Shenwu approved of it; because the multitude's counsels differed, he ceased.
idiomatic: Gao Huan approved — but because the council could not agree, he dropped the pursuit.

literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jinmen Commandery.
idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as duke of Jinmen Commandery.

literal: When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, he garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang succeeded to power, he held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.

literal: At the time the emperor, because the walled fort built by Huai Province Governor Ping Jian and others lay deep in enemy territory, wished to abandon it; Le, holding that Zhiguan Pass was a strategic strongpoint that must be defended, thereupon repaired it further, added troops and commanders, returned to garrison Heyang, and was appointed Minister of Works.
idiomatic: The emperor wished to abandon fortifications built by Huai Province governor Ping Jian and others, because they lay deep in enemy territory. Pan Le argued that Zhiguan Pass was a vital strongpoint and had to be held; he repaired the works, posted more troops and officers, returned to garrison Heyang, and was appointed minister of works.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, Le presented the seal and cord.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Pan Le presented the imperial seal and cord.

literal: Advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Hedong Commandery; transferred to Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: He was advanced to Prince of Hedong Commandery and transferred to minister over the masses.

literal: Zhou Wen marched east to Xiao and Shan, dispatching his field headquarters Houmochen Chong from Qizi Ridge toward Zhiguan, while Yitong Yang Piao by the Guchong road out toward Jian Province captured Gugong garrison.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched east to Xiao and Shan, sending field headquarters Houmochen Chong from Qizi Ridge against Zhiguan Pass while yitong Yang Piao by the Guchong road into Jian Province captured the Gugong garrison.

literal: An edict ordered Le to command the great host to resist.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Pan Le to take overall command and meet the invasion.

literal: Le marched day and night without pause; reaching Changzi, he dispatched Yitong Han Yongxing west from Jian Province toward Chong, and Chong thereupon fled.
idiomatic: Pan Le forced the march day and night as far as Changzi, sent yitong Han Yongxing west from Jian Province against Houmochen Chong — and Chong fled.

literal: Again made Grand Governor of the Southern Route, to campaign against Hou Jing.
idiomatic: He was again made grand governor of the south route and sent against Hou Jing.

literal: Le set out from Shibie, marched south over a hundred li, and reached Liang's Jing Province.
idiomatic: Pan Le marched out from Shibie, drove south more than a hundred li, and reached Jing Province in Liang territory.

literal: Jing Province had formerly been at Shiliang; Hou Jing had changed it to Huai Province. Le recovered the territory, re-established Jing Province, and also captured An Province.
idiomatic: Jing Province had stood at Shiliang until Hou Jing renamed it Huai Province. Pan Le recovered the ground, restored Jing Province, and also took An Province.

literal: Appointed Governor of Ying Province; still raided Huai and Han.
idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Ying Province and continued to carry the war into the Huai and Han country.

literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanchi.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanchi.

literal: Posthumously granted Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, grand marshal, and director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: His son Zihuan succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Zihuan succeeded to the line.

literal: The sons of the various generals were mostly arrogant and unrestrained; Zihuan was deep, meticulous, cautious and reverent, holding himself to purity and restraint.
idiomatic: The sons of the great generals were mostly proud and undisciplined; Zihuan was grave, careful, and dutiful, claiming only quiet integrity for himself.

literal: Married the princess; appointed Commandant of Attendants for the Son-in-Law.
idiomatic: He married an imperial princess and was appointed commandant of the emperor's son-in-law.

literal: At the end of Wuping, he served as Right Vice Director of the You Province Circuit Field Headquarters and Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he served as right vice director of the You Province circuit field headquarters and governor of You Province.

literal: When Zhou armies were about to enter Ye, Zihuan led tens of thousands of picked cavalry to go to the relief.
idiomatic: When Northern Zhou armies were closing on Ye, Zihuan led tens of thousands of picked cavalry to the relief.

literal: Reaching Baling, learning that Ye could not be held, he went to Ji Province and surrendered.
idiomatic: He reached Baling, learned that Ye could not be held, and went to Ji Province to surrender.

literal: Zhou granted Upper Opening Establishment.
idiomatic: Zhou granted him an upper opening establishment.

literal: In the early Daye era of Sui he died.
idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Daye era under Sui.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
